status: PUB-9C PASS-03 BATCH 5 — VERIFIED AUTHORITY EXPANSION
policy: Authorities support retained physical state and altered later response only. Memory terminology does not imply awareness, recollection, intelligence, or consciousness.

records.citation: Netea, Mihai G., Leo A. B. Joosten, Eicke Latz, Kingston H. G. Mills, Gioacchino Natoli, Hendrik G. Stunnenberg, Luke A. J. O’Neill, and Ramnik J. Xavier. 2016. ‘Trained Immunity: A Program of Innate Immune Memory in Health and Disease.’ Science 352 (6284): aaf1098. https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aaf1098.
records.whatThisSourceSupports: Innate immune systems can exhibit history-dependent altered responses associated with persistent functional, metabolic, and epigenetic reprogramming, conventionally termed trained immunity.
records.whatThisSourceDoesNotSupport: It does not establish conscious recollection, semantic memory, a mind outside nervous systems, or civilization-scale memory as an organism-level property.
records.whereMacroscopicLifeGoesBeyondIt: Macroscopic Life uses trained immunity as a calibration case for physically retained state becoming causally available later, while requiring separate evidence for candidate-level Memory Turnover.

records.citation: Liu, Ning, and Caroline Dean. 2018. ‘Epigenetic Environmental Memories in Plants: Establishment, Maintenance, and Reprogramming.’ Trends in Genetics 34 (11): 856–866. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tig.2018.07.006.
records.whatThisSourceSupports: Some environmental exposures in plants can induce chromatin-associated states that persist after the initiating signal and alter later gene expression or response; maintenance and reprogramming are part of the phenomenon.
records.whatThisSourceDoesNotSupport: It does not establish conscious memory, plant phenomenology, universal inheritance of acquired states, or a single substrate shared by plant, immune, neural, and civilizational memory.
records.whereMacroscopicLifeGoesBeyondIt: Macroscopic Life abstracts the narrower comparative requirement that a physically retained state must later re-enter causal processing and alter a response.

cautions.chapter10: TRACE ≠ STORAGE ≠ FUNCTIONAL MEMORY ≠ CONSCIOUS RECOLLECTION. Cross-system comparison is functional and mechanistic, not a claim of substrate identity or awareness.
